script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel.

NORTH AMERICA
The Caribbean - bottom line: JoZee finds her reggae calling with ‘Who God Says I Am’.
- Jamaica Observer, 2 hours ago: JoZee finds her reggae calling with ‘Who God Says I Am’.
Gospel artiste JoZee grew up in Chicago with Sicily in her blood—but Jamaica has been beating in her heart for decades. Now the Italian-American is turning a childhood obsession with reggae into a full-circle musical moment with Who God Says I Am, her first reggae gospel album, produced by veteran Jamaican hitmaker Danny Brownie for Main Street Records. The 15-track project, due October 6, 2026, explores faith, identity and the deceptively simple question at its core: Who does God say I am? For JoZee, reggae isn't a new experiment.
- Jamaica Observer, 2 hours ago: Montego Bay to install flood sensors through international grant support.
ST JAMES, Jamaica — Montego Bay is set to strengthen its flood-monitoring and early warning capabilities after being selected for a US$3.5-million grant programme supported by the Mayors Migration Council’s (MMC) Global Cities Fund for Migrants and Refugees. Mayor of Montego Bay Councillor Richard Vernon, who is currently overseas attending the conference, said the city is one of 10 selected for this year’s programme. According to Vernon, the funding will be used to develop an early warning system designed to give residents more time to respond to rising floodwaters.
- Jamaica Observer, 3 hours ago: Iley Dread celebrates 31 years of Kings Of Kings Productions with new album.
At the time Colin “Iley Dread” Levy started Kings Of Kings Productions in Montreal in 1995, Canada had no record company promoting reggae on the scale of VP Records in the United States or Greensleeves in the United Kingdom. Iley Dread, who is from St James, will be in Jamaica to celebrate his birthday on December 16, with an event at Louise Bennett Garden Theatre in Kingston. It will also mark his company’s 31st anniversary and the release of Upliftment, the singer-producer’s sixth album. He is proud of Kings Of Kings Productions’ achievements. “It has surpassed expectations.
- Jamaica Observer, 3 hours ago: Grade seven Mount Alvernia High students excels in 2026 CSEC exams.
KINGSTON, Jamaica — Long before Mount Alvernia High School student in Montego Bay, St James, Kenya Gardener, sat her first Caribbean Secondary Education Certificate (CSEC) examinations in the May/June 2026 sitting, her mother had been teaching her lessons that extended beyond the syllabus: how to stay organised, believe in her abilities and approach her studies with consistency and discipline.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel.
The United States on Sunday warned that fighting between Saudi Arabia and Houthis could “escalate rapidly” after a missile attack targeted Riyadh for the first time since the Yemen conflict resumed. “This military conflict has the potential to escalate rapidly,” the US State Department warned, adding American citizens outside the Middle East should “seriously reconsider travel to and through the region”. US President Donald Trump also cut short a weekend at Camp David, a secluded presidential complex in rural Maryland, to return unexpectedly to the White House on Saturday.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 16 hours ago: Turkiye says it could help meet Saudi Arabia’s military needs.
ANKARA: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said on Saturday that Saudi Arabia may have military needs due to the ongoing attacks by Yemen’s Houthis and that Turkiye was ready to help under a trilateral defence pact that includes Pakistan. “We see there are very serious attacks on Saudi Arabia’s territorial integrity, sovereignty. We have an alliance agreement in our pact. We are in serious solidarity on this point. They may have some military needs, especially on some technical issues. We would have no issues in meeting these,” Fidan told broadcaster NTV.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: Two officers among 6 martyred, 8 terrorists killed in Hangu fire exchange: ISPR.
Two officers and four others were martyred while eight terrorists were killed in a fire exchange in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Hangu district on Sunday, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. During an intense fire exchange between a “security forces convoy and Khwarij”, 23-year-old Captain Abuzar Farooq from Gujranwala and 22-year-old Lieutenant Sheraz Babar of Chakwal, “who were leading their troops from the front, fought gallantly and paid the ultimate sacrifice and embraced martyrdom along with their four men”.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 14 hours ago: Security forces kill 5 terrorists, recover 23 abductees in operation along N-25 highway near Balochistan's Kalat: ISPR.
Security forces have killed five terrorists and recovered 23 kidnapped individuals from their hideout during an operation along the N-25 Karachi-Chaman highway near Balochistan’s Kalat, the military’s media affairs wing said on Sunday. In a statement, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said that terrorists belonging to Fitna-al-Hindustan tried to disrupt people’s movement by establishing a checkpost for abduction for ransom, extortion and snatching of vehicles along the N-25 highway, also knows as the Pakistan Expressway, on the night between Sept 18 and Sept 19.

Ukraine fired waves of drones at Moscow and the surrounding region on the final day of voting, killing two people and setting an oil refinery ablaze, officials said. Russia’s defence ministry accused Ukraine of attempting to “disrupt the democratic will of Russian citizens”...

Long-time Slovak leader Fico, who has kept up warm relations with Russia and refuses military aid for Ukraine, said this week that Europe was closer than ever to a large-scale war ‌erupting from the Ukraine war. - Times of India - Top Stories, 8 hours ago: ‘Path of deception closed’: Iran vows ‘no limits’ in retaliation if US attacks.
Iran has issued a stern warning, promising unlimited retaliation and a decisive conflict if the US attacks or dismisses its demands. Through Qatari mediators, Tehran has proposed seven conditions for a truce to Washington. Officials in Iran stressed that any regional nations supporting the US would be drawn into the conflict. Parliament speaker Ghalibaf reiterated the dual approach of military readiness alongside diplomatic negotiations.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 4 hours ago: ‘When do I blow entire nation up?' Trump's ultimatum after Iran warns of 'decisive war'.
President Trump warned Iran of serious consequences if it does not change course. He outlined options including destruction, economic collapse, or diplomacy with Iran. Iran's command stated any US attack would face retaliation without limitations. Iran relayed truce conditions to the US through Qatari mediators. Trump signaled openness to talks with Iranian President Pezeshkian.

Dylan Young’s sound recalls the Beach Boys and the Beatles, both contemporary and timeless – and his latest album Massive Shoe is attracting international acclaim It’s been a huge couple of years for Way Dynamic, the Melbourne multi-instrumentalist whose real name is Dylan Young. His 2025 album Massive Shoe is about to be re-released internationally after Young signed with the indie giant Jagjaguwar. The likes of Elton John, Djo, Zane Lowe and Elijah Wood have sung his praises. Last year he opened for Black Country New Road, Waxahatchee and MJ Lenderman on their Australian tours.
